cards.explanation: The answer is that everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God. The writer says, “Everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.” Love comes from God, and the ones who love carry His family name. Born, not hired, friends. Nobody fills out an application for that.

The answer is False. The writer says, “Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.” He doesn't leave a loophole in there, friends. He even gives the reason right in the verse: God is love.

The answer is that He sent His one and only Son into the world. God's love was revealed when He sent His one and only Son into the world, so that we might live through Him. The writer points to a Person, not a program, friends. Love showed up with a name and an address.

The answer is not that we loved God, but that He loved us. It's baked right into the verse, friends: “not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.” Love starts on His side, not ours. We're catching up, not leading the way.

The answer is sins. God sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins. The writer names the real problem out loud and then names what God did about it, friends. I'd call that love with its sleeves rolled up.

The answer is that God remains in us and His love is perfected in us. No one has ever seen God, but the writer says that if we love one another, God remains in us, and His love is perfected in us. That's a mighty big thing to say about loving one another, friends.

The answer is that He has given us of His Spirit. The writer says, “By this we know that we remain in Him, and He in us: He has given us of His Spirit.” The proof isn't something we produce, friends. It's something He gave.

The answer is True. The verse says, “If anyone confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God.” Notice the word anyone, friends. The writer keeps it open to whoever confesses.
The answer is love. “God is love; whoever abides in love abides in God, and God in him.” To abide means to stay put, to make a home, friends. And here the home is love.
The answer is confidence. Love is perfected among us so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment. The writer says confidence, friends, and that's the word to hold onto.

The answer is that in this world we are just like Him. The writer says, “for in this world we are just like Him.” The confidence comes from being like Him, friends, not from a spotless record. That's all the verse says, so I'll leave it right there.

The answer is that perfect love drives fear right out. The writer says, “…perfect love drives out fear…” Driven out, friends, like a squatter getting the boot. When perfect love moves in, fear doesn't get a vote. That's the verb he picked, and I love it.

The answer is True. The writer gives the reason right there: “…because fear involves punishment.” He doesn't go on to explain more, friends, so I won't either. He says there is no fear in love, and that's the reason he gives.
The answer is a liar. The writer doesn't tiptoe, friends: “but hates his brother, he is a liar.” That's a strong word. He's looking at what a person says next to how that person treats his brother.

The answer is False. The writer says, “For anyone who does not love his brother, whom he has seen, cannot love God, whom he has not seen.” The one who doesn't love the brother he can see cannot love God, friends. That's what the verse says.

The answer is a commandment from Him. “And we have this commandment from Him: Whoever loves God must love his brother as well.” It comes straight from Him, friends. It's a commandment, not a suggestion.
